evals.name: start-new-work-full
evals.prompt:
We're starting a new project. Our gym owner sent this in Slack, get us going:

"ok so members need to book classes on their phone, and cancel up to 2h before or they get charged. coaches should see who's coming. we have 3 sites now, maybe 5 next year. it HAS to be live before the january rush (dec 1). we use stripe already for memberships so payments should go through that. maybe some analytics later on attendance? oh and it should be fast, people complain the current thing is slow"
evals.expected_output: One design doc in docs/design/ with Status: Draft, requirements, scope, conceptual and logical design, a decisions log and a build plan, then a stop asking for approval with no code written.
expectations: The reply's first line states the size of the work (Full, or equivalent)
Exactly one design doc is written under docs/design/, and its first lines include a 'Status: Draft' line
The Requirements section has numbered sources and FR/NFR/CON IDs, and every Must and Should FR has an acceptance criterion
'maybe 5 next year' and 'maybe some analytics' are open questions or Later items, not silently ruled Out
A Scope section lists In, Out and Later
The design has a context map marking at least one trust boundary, and a data ownership table where every datum has one named owner
At least one scenario walkthrough names the contract or operation called at each hop
'it should be fast' becomes a numeric NFR with a mechanism, or an open question asking for the number
Pivotal choices are recorded as numbered D-n entries with context, options and choice inside the doc, and no separate ADR file is created
A build plan lists slices, each with the requirement IDs it delivers
No implementation code is written, and the reply asks the user to approve the doc, leading with open questions

evals.name: start-new-work-small
evals.prompt: Let's add a dark mode toggle to the settings page that remembers the choice.
evals.expected_output: A short Draft design doc that reads the existing code, keeps sections small, plans one or two slices and asks for approval before changing code.
expectations: The reply's first line states the work is small
One design doc is written under docs/design/ with a 'Status: Draft' line, and it is under 90 lines
Remembering the choice is its own requirement with an acceptance criterion
The design reuses the existing settings storage in app.js (the notes.settings localStorage key or loadSettings/saveSettings)
Scope lists In, Out and Later (one line each is fine)
No section is left empty or padded with 'none' rows
The build plan has one or two slices
No app file (app.js, settings.html, style.css, index.html) is changed, and the reply asks for approval

evals.name: trivial-fix-no-doc
evals.prompt: Fix the typo in the README's settings section.
evals.expected_output: Says it is trivial and needs no design doc, fixes 'recieve' to 'receive', and changes nothing else.
expectations: The reply says the change is trivial and needs no design doc
No file is created under docs/design/
README.md now says 'receive' instead of 'recieve'
No other file in the project is changed

evals.name: build-first-slice
evals.prompt: The class booking design (docs/design/class-booking.md) is approved. Go ahead and build slice 1.
evals.expected_output: Slice 1's detailed design added to the doc, booking implemented with the transactional capacity check from D-1, passing tests for each slice-1 acceptance criterion, and the doc's status, plan, verification table and change log updated.
expectations: The doc gains a 'Slice 1' detailed design section with the book operation's signature, at least one literal example call and result, and the error cases 'class full' and 'already booked'
The implementation enforces capacity inside one transaction with a conditional update (or equivalent), as decision D-1 requires, plus a unique constraint on (member, slot)
There are tests for FR-1, FR-4 and NFR-3, including one with concurrent or interleaved booking attempts on the last place
All tests pass when the grader runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` in the project
The Verification table has a row per slice-1 acceptance criterion with a test name and a result
The status line reads 'Building (slice 1 of 3)' or equivalent, and slice 1 is marked done in the build plan
A change-log line describes the slice-1 work
No cancel or fee code (slices 2 and 3) is implemented

evals.name: scope-change-on-existing-doc
evals.prompt: Members keep asking for a waitlist when a class is full. Can we add one?
evals.expected_output: Finds and updates the existing design doc rather than creating a new one, brings the waitlist into scope with a requirement, design changes and a plan slice, and asks for approval before building.
expectations: The existing docs/design/class-booking.md is updated and no second design doc is created
The waitlist becomes an FR (FR-5 or a new ID) with an acceptance criterion and moves from Later into In
The design is updated for the waitlist, including how promotion from the waitlist keeps NFR-3 (no overbooking) true
A new D-n decision or a new build-plan slice covers the waitlist
The doc's status returns to Draft (or the reply explicitly asks for approval of the changed scope) and no waitlist code is written
A change-log line records the scope change
